definitions.explanation: A vivid, deep blue color. Originally refers to the color of the pigment ultramarine, derived from the mineral lapis lazuli.

examples.japanese: {空|そら}が{群青色|ぐんじょういろ}に{染|そ}まった。
examples.english: The sky was stained deep blue.

examples.japanese: {群青色|ぐんじょういろ}の{海|うみ}がとても{美|うつく}しかった。
examples.english: The ultramarine sea was very beautiful.

examples.japanese: {日本画|にほんが}では{群青色|ぐんじょういろ}は{伝統的|でんとうてき}な{顔料|がんりょう}として{使|つか}われてきた。
examples.english: In Japanese painting, ultramarine has been used as a traditional pigment.

notes:
A compound of {群青|ぐんじょう} (ultramarine pigment) + {色|いろ} (color). {群青|ぐんじょう} alone can also refer to the color, but adding {色|いろ} makes it explicitly a color name.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {群青色|ぐんじょういろ}の{空|そら}: ultramarine sky
- {群青色|ぐんじょういろ}の{海|うみ}: deep blue sea
- {群青色|ぐんじょういろ}に{輝|かがや}く: to shine in deep blue

CULTURAL NOTE:
Ultramarine ({群青|ぐんじょう}) is one of the traditional Japanese colors ({日本|にほん}の{伝統色|でんとうしょく}), historically valued in Japanese painting ({日本画|にほんが}). The pigment was originally made from the mineral {瑠璃|るり} (lapis lazuli).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {紺色|こんいろ}: navy blue, dark blue — a darker, more muted blue
- {藍色|あいいろ}: indigo — a blue derived from plant-based indigo dye
- {瑠璃色|るりいろ}: lapis lazuli blue — similar vivid blue, named after the mineral itself
